question: What are these firms saying about AI in advice delivery, and who is claiming the most?

claims.text: AI in advice delivery - Edward Jones: not found in the evidence provided. The Edward Jones filings in the evidence describe AI only as an industry and competitive development, not as something the firm uses in advice delivery.

AI in advice delivery - Bank of America (Merrill's parent): On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CEO Brian Moynihan said that in wealth management and other relationship-manager businesses AI is helping relationship managers and advisors search and summarize information, preparing them to deliver personalized planning and pitches to clients, and that copilots help organize prospecting. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), the CFO said the GWIM segment (Merrill plus the Private Bank) benefited from new AI-enabled tools that help advisers prepare for client conversations, identify opportunities and deliver more personalized advice at scale.

AI in advice delivery - Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), the CFO cited early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot, including LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors. On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said the firm's growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base.

AI in advice delivery - Raymond James: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm rolled out a solution called Ray that advisers and sales assistants use to sift through information and find answers to complicated questions, piloted with a few hundred advisers. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said the enterprise rollout of the proprietary AI assistant Raimond was completed, giving staff a secure, plain-language way to access institutional knowledge. The June 2025 investor-day deck lists AI pipeline items including client portfolio analyses and meeting and CRM notes management.

AI in advice delivery - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said AI can help create personalized, deeper relationships with clients the firm cannot serve at scale one-to-one, and described Portfolio Insights, an AI-enabled experience giving clients tailored insights on their portfolios. Schwab's 3Q26 release (October 2026) lists the launch of Charley, an AI-powered assistant giving U.S. retail clients conversational access to Schwab's tools, and a partnership with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs Schwab serves. Schwab's 2Q26 release (July 2026) describes Portfolio Insights as a generative AI feature that is not investment advice and may be inaccurate.

Productivity and capacity - Edward Jones: not found in the evidence provided. The 10-Qs attribute higher communications and data processing expense to investments in new tools and technology, but do not tie it to AI or to advisor productivity.

Productivity and capacity - Bank of America (Merrill's parent): On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Moynihan said 17,000 programmers use AI coding technology, saving 10-15% in code generation costs, and that the bank is beginning to see AI aiding efficiency. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said the tools are designed to help customer relationship managers prepare more thoroughly for client meetings, and the CFO said AI-enabled tools are more embedded in workflows, including client-facing teams, reducing manual work.

Productivity and capacity - Morgan Stanley: advisor-specific productivity or meeting-preparation claims are not found in the evidence provided. Management's statements are enterprise-wide: on the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Pick said firms will spend several points running on being more efficient, and that over time more productive, with AI.

Productivity and capacity - Raymond James: The June 2025 investor-day deck lists Zoom AI Meeting Summaries and GenAI search among advisor tools, and an AI framework goal to integrate AI tools into the advisor platform to reduce administrative workload. In April 2026 Shoukry said the firm is increasing AI integration to improve efficiency and give professionals more time for clients. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026) he said savings of advisers' administrative time let them spend more time on relationships, adding that the firm tells advisers "AI will not replace advisers. Advisers who use AI will replace advisers who do not use AI."

Productivity and capacity - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster described a tool that summarizes past client interactions before a meeting, records the meeting and prepares an action-based summary, which he said the firm believes will make financial consultants more productive and able to serve more clients. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026) he said developer team productivity improved 15% to 20% over the past year; on the 3Q26 call (October 2026) he said about 25%.
Quantified claims - Edward Jones: no AI-specific results, adoption or investment figures are found in the evidence provided.

Quantified claims - Bank of America (Merrill's parent): On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Moynihan said more than 200,000 teammates are using AI-enabled capabilities, generating more than 400,000 prompts a day, with over 300 AI use cases approved, all with good economics, 114 live generative AI use cases and 34 fully implemented. The 3Q26 release (October 2026) says that with more than 200,000 teammates using AI tools and 300-plus approved use cases, "we are turning our scale into a competitive advantage." The November 2025 investor-day deck states 100% of Private Bank teammates have access to AI tools. These figures are enterprise-wide, not Merrill-only.

Quantified claims - Morgan Stanley: no AI-specific figures are found in the evidence provided. On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Pick said confidence in the efficiency and effectiveness potential of AI-related technologies increases each quarter, and on the 3Q26 call (October 2026) the CFO said AI-related technology investments position the firm to strengthen its competitive moats.

Quantified claims - Raymond James: The October 2025 release says the firm made significant investments of approximately $1 billion in technology including AI during the fiscal year and created the roles of Chief AI Officer and Head of AI Strategy. On the 1Q26 and 2Q26 calls (April and July 2026), Shoukry cited $1.1 billion spent on technology (and AI), said AI will differentiate firms, and that smaller firms cannot keep up with that level of investment.

Quantified claims - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster said every one of the firm's 33,000 employees has AI tools. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), he said developer productivity is up about 25%, that 77% of U.S. investors use AI while more than 90% prefer human involvement alongside it, and that the combination of people, technology, scale and value is a powerful advantage that is very difficult to replicate.

Overall - who claims the most: the quantified claims are on different metrics: use cases, prompts and live deployments at Bank of America; technology dollars at Raymond James; developer-productivity percentages and employee tool access at Schwab. The evidence does not support a like-for-like ranking, and Edward Jones and Morgan Stanley make no comparable AI-specific figures in the evidence.

Future of advice and risks - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published March 2026) states that the industry is seeing more firms use artificial intelligence technologies and lower-cost computer-based "robo-advice", which has required and is expected to require significant investments, and that the firm competes with robo-advisors and lower-cost options. It says use of AI by the firm or its third parties may expose it to additional information-security and legal risk, increased regulation and regulatory scrutiny, and reputational harm, and lists AI among the strategic risks it addresses through its initiatives.

Future of advice and risks - Bank of America (Merrill's parent): On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), Moynihan said the bank's view of AI is "enhanced intelligence, not an artificial intelligence" and that teammates remain critical to delivering services. The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) says expanded AI use, including autonomous AI agents, may increase data risk, control failures and operational, legal and regulatory risk, and that AI-related laws and regulations are rapidly evolving.

Future of advice and risks - Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Pick said the continuous "arms race of one AI platform versus another" is additive to the firm's technology, and that the best trusted advisers sitting with the client are "the secret sauce", including the wealth management financial adviser. The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) says the firm's ability to compete across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels is affected by its technology supporting client needs, including generative AI.

Future of advice and risks - Raymond James: On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), Shoukry said leadership has conviction that AI will be a game changer but it is still too early to know how it will play out. The 2025 10-K (published November 2025) warns that inaccurate or biased AI output, privacy and security risks and new AI regulation could harm the business and add cost, and notes state and EU AI rules. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said the firm tells advisers AI will not replace advisers, and that investment requirements make the industry moat increase.

Future of advice and risks - Schwab: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said 77% of U.S. investors use AI today while more than 90% prefer human involvement alongside it, that relationships and trust still matter, and that AI has to be safe and secure; he said the firm is blocking unauthorized agents that try to log in on behalf of clients. The July 2026 release cautions that generative AI output may be inaccurate.

adjacent.text: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Morgan Stanley's CFO said AI tools used by salespeople in the equities business show productivity that "is real" and that is where much of the spend is being seen.
adjacent.differs_because: It describes the equities (institutional) business, not advisor productivity in wealth management.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones' communications and data processing expense rose 19% to $317 in 1Q26, which the 10-Q attributes to investments in new tools and technology and related depreciation.
adjacent.differs_because: The expense is not identified as AI spending and is not an AI result or adoption figure.

adjacent.text: Industry estimates cited by Deloitte (May 2026) say 73% of advisory firms use AI in some capacity, 6% use agentic tools and 5% have implemented cross-system AI integration.
adjacent.differs_because: It is an industry-wide research estimate, not a claim by any of the firms asked about.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (September 2026) reported that Shoukry said Raymond James's AI-powered advisor assistant Raimond, in pilot, was trained on approximately one million recorded advisor-service-center calls.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.
